done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json leave out stories, tasks and fixes that were merged or done more than 7 days ago (they still show in the text board's history), with no cache; their output is otherwise unchanged; a command test on a repo with old finished items shows they are left out and that the number of git commands per call does not grow with them (no wall-clock timing); tests/test_machine_views.py stays within its time limit on Windows CI; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body: The Done-when requirement remains incomplete: the proof list explicitly says a successful Windows run of the repaired branch is still required. The supplied close run passes only the four new retention/client cases, while the broader machine-view pass was local. The limits in tests/conftest.py:167 and .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:42,58 remain enforced, but they do not establish that the repaired branch passes within them. Supply a successful Windows CI run covering tests/test_machine_views.py.
findings.title: Not done: tests/test_machine_views.py stays within its time limit on Windows CI

findings.body: The previously reported defect remains. For a signed landed commit, log.showSignature=true makes this git show include signature-verification output ([Git configuration documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-logshowSignature)). src/forge/repo.py:144 returns the entire trimmed stdout, which board.py:575 embeds into diff-tree input as a tree ID. This corrupts the snapshot batch used by both JSON commands and the human board. Use rev-parse <ref>^{tree}, or explicitly disable signature output.
findings.title: Disable signature output when reading the landed tree ID

findings.body: The previously reported defect remains: dates includes historical additions whose state files no longer exist in landed_states, and this comprehension expires those paths anyway. After reverting an old fix merge and removing its refs, src/forge/task.py:273 permits restarting the same slug because _merged checks current file existence at task.py:219–221. Tasks can likewise restart through task.py:189. The new ongoing item is then omitted from both JSON views; next also suppresses fix guidance at nextstep.py:209. Require the path to exist in landed_states before expiring it from a historical merge date.
findings.title: Do not expire restarted tasks and fixes using reverted merge dates

why: forge board --json takes about 45 seconds and forge next --json about 10, so the pane's 10-second refresh would keep a core busy in every open Claude Code session
